Hi team - tagging in a quick worked example and the assumptions we typically use for marketplace private-offer math. I've attached an initial draft of the private offer language (aws-private-offer-draft.pdf) and updated the pricing-model.xlsx with sample calculations.

High-level mapping (short)
- Redwood hosted price: quoted as $ per token (we typically think in $ per 1k tokens or $ per 1M tokens for procurement).
- Marketplace private offer: the customer sees the private-offer line item as the charge. That line item should reflect the final customer-facing price (includes Redwood price + marketplace fee + any reseller margin).

Worked example (round numbers)
- Redwood base cost to serve (estimate): $300 per 1M tokens (this includes model and infra amortized cost; internal floor).
- Redwood target margin: 10% -> $30 per 1M tokens.
- Marketplace fee (AWS/GCP/Azure typical): 12-15% of the line item. For a target customer price P, fee = P * 15%.

We want to solve for P such that: P = base_cost + margin + fee_on_P 
=> P = 300 + 30 + 0.15 * P 
=> P - 0.15P = 330 
=> 0.85P = 330 
=> P = 330 / 0.85 = $388.

So in this example the customer-facing private-offer unit price works out to ~$388 per 1M tokens. That meets the lower end of BrightCart's stated range and leaves a small buffer. If BrightCart needs $350/1M at scale, we'd need to reduce base cost (model selection, quantization) or accept a lower margin.

What we recommend
- Target private-offer price: $380-$420 per 1M tokens (this assumes a 10% Redwood margin and a 12-15% marketplace fee).
- For committed volumes (>=1B tokens/year), we can talk volume-based tiering that brings base_cost down and target price to the $300-$350/1M band.

I've attached a short draft of the private-offer line item text and an editable workbook. Happy to walk through numbers on the call with AWS + BrightCart.

Attachments: aws-private-offer-draft.pdf
